newsitem.title: INDIA: India ITC officials enter directorate.
newsitem.headline: India ITC officials enter directorate.

text.p: ITC Ltd chairman Yogesh Deveshwar and former chairman K.L. Chugh entered Indian Enforcement Directorate offices on Thursday, witnesses said.

Witnesses saw Deveshwar and Chugh enter the eastern regional office of the Enforcement Directorate in central Calcutta, a day after the government announced an investigation into alleged foreign exchange rule violations by the cigarette maker.
Deveshwar and Chugh declined to comment when reporters outside the Enforcement Directorate's offices asked them about the investigation.
Directorate officials said Chugh had been questioned on Wednesday in New Delhi before arriving in Calcutta, where the tobacco company has its headquarters.
"We are investigating the matter," an investigating officer who asked not to be identified told reporters outside the directorate's offices.

"The investigation will continue and we are not in a position now to tell you anything," the investigating officer said. He would not comment on Deveshwar and Chugh's appearance at the Enforcement Directorate.
Earlier on Thursday, a senior directorate official said Deveshwar was being interrogated and his house had been searched in the morning.
On Wednesday the Enforcement Directorate arrested a director and three former officials of ITC for alleged violation of foreign exchange rules.

The directorate, the watchdog over issues related to corporate finances, made the arrests during early morning searches of offices and homes in four cities -- Calcutta, Bombay, Hyderabad and New Delhi.

The Finance Ministry said in a statement on Wednesday that the search operations were undertaken "only after sufficient evidence had been collected indicating FERA (Foreign Exchange Regulation Act) violations by ITC Ltd to the tune of over $100 million".
ITC has not yet commented publicly on the investigation.
ITC is 31.7 percent controlled by Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc. The rest of its shares are held by Indian financial institutions and the public.
